articles.title: Next NFL champion will be decided by newest rivalry - Rams vs. Seahawks
articles.summary: The Super Bowl champion Seahawks are being hunted by the Rams, the team they beat in the NFC championship game. The Rams are building what some call a Super...
articles.body:
The NFL , like most leagues, has a long history of bitter rivals, going way back to Green Bay-Chicago, and progressing through Dallas-Washington, Pittsburgh-Baltimore, New England-Indianapolis, and more recently, Kansas City-Buffalo. And there are plenty more.

But what we have brewing on the West Coast could be just as tasty.

The Super Bowl champion Seahawks are being hunted by the Rams, the team they beat in the NFC championship game. The Rams are building what some are labeling a Super Team. L.A. has added to an already stacked offense by trading for Myles Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, and cornerback Trent McDuffie and welcoming back a three-time DPOY, Aaron Donald.

And none of this was lost on the Seahawks. Safety Nick Emmanwori trolled the Rams after Donald's return with a four-word post that read: "All that for us," and included a pair of sarcastic emojis.

The Seahawks are not resting after winning their second Lombardi Trophy. Perhaps feeling a bit pressured to respond to the Rams and take a risk, Seattle signing troubled cornerback Terrion Arnold, released by the Lions after being arrested on eight felony charges.

All of which should make for a doozy of a race in the NFC West. The problem is the schedule. The NFL made sure this rivalry would receive the longest build-up in history by scheduling their first meeting Christmas Day. They see each other for the second time two weeks later - on the last day of the regular season.

One more game likely awaits. With any luck, it's three weeks later for the right to play in the Super Bowl.

Until then, we are here to sort out the NFL season with your Super Bowl hopefuls, playoff contenders and the bottom feeders. Teams are mentioned on order of how we rank them.

Bills, Eagles among Super Bowl contenders

The Los Angeles Rams (1) had the best offseason in the league, by far. Garrett, McDuffie and Donald are a huge boost to a defense that was solid, but not great. Add that to the most potent offense in the league with QB Matthew Stafford, WRs Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, and RB Kyren Williams, and no wonder the Seattle Seahawks (2) are paying attention.

Seattle's John Schneider, the reigning Executive of the Year, overcame the unavoidable departures that happen when a team wins the Super Bowl by making Jaxon Smith-Njigba the highest paid receiver in NFL history and Devon Witherspoon the highest paid cornerback in NFL history. Remember, winning consecutive Super Bowls is rare. Happened just twice this century.

The list of teams entering the season in the category of Super Bowl or Bust is led by the Buffalo Bills (3) . The Bills took a gut punch in 2025 with finally seeing the one team that has prevented them from playing in the Super Bowl in recent years, the Chiefs, take a nosedive and then watching the Patriots re-emerge and return to the title game.

The Bills are counting on a few changes at the top, including a new head coach (Joe Brady) and defensive coordinator (Jim Leonhard) to help them get over the top. And they still have QB Josh Allen, who always gives them a chance.

The Philadelphia Eagles (4) are hoping for addition by subtraction on offense. Trading A.J. Brown, a three-time All Pro still in his prime, gives QB Jalen Hurts a new No. 1 receiver, DeVonta Smith, and the team less drama. The defense is led by the group that can get to the quarterback and keep teams out of the end zone. But will it all be enough to overcome the Rams and Seahawks in the NFC?

The AFC has a long list of teams capable of extending the Bills' misery, including the team that did it last year, the Denver Broncos (5) . The Broncos likely would have been in the Super Bowl if not for QB Bo Nix being injured in the Broncos overtime win over Buffalo in the divisional round. The Broncos will ride with their defense and giving Nix another weapon in ex-Dolphin Jaylen Waddle helps, too.

The New England Patriots (6) reboot is real with QB Drake Maye's impressive breakout year. Maye now has Brown as a No. 1 target. The Pats need the defense to dominate the way it did last year against a much tougher schedule. Speaking of defense, no team will be more reliant on that side of the ball than the Houston Texans (7) , who roll out a unit led by Will Anderson Jr. and added Jadeveon Clowney for depth. C.J. Stroud cannot crash and burn again on the playoffs if the Texans want to compete.

The Baltimore Ravens (8) and Detroit Lions (9) are two teams whose Super Bowl window is closing, but still showing some light. The Ravens' hopes center around QB Lamar Jackson staying healthy and the defense getting its mojo back after adding edge defender Trey Hendrickson. Like the Ravens, the Lions schedule is very forgiving and their offense is loaded with QB Jared Goff, WR Amon-Ra St. Brown, RB Jahmyr Gibbs and OT Penei Sewell. The pass defense needs to improve.

Finally, we get to the team that entered last year having played in five of the last six Super Bowls, winning three. Needless to say, the Kansas City Chiefs (10) need Patrick Mahomes to be healthy and the defense to improve to resemble what it was during that dominant decade. Injuries also will determine if the San Francisco 49ers (11) have a chance of staying close in a division that includes the Rams and Seahawks. QB Brock Purdy has become pretty relevant, but he was just one key piece to deal with injuries last season. Not to be overlooked are the off-season distractions of the owner's arrest and the head coach's auto accident.

Can Chargers (and Mike McDaniel), Jaguars sneak into playoffs?

Los Angeles Chargers (12) offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is working with Justin Herbert, the QB he should have had in Miami. Herbert is a two-time Pro Bowler who has yet to win a playoff game. Jim Harbaugh hopes McDaniel can help change that. The Cincinnati Bengals (13) have a QB in Joe Burrow who led them to the Super Bowl in 2021, but haven't done much since, missing the playoffs the last three years. The offense is good enough for a Super Bowl contender. The defense probably not.

The Jacksonville Jaguars (14) still believe in QB Trevor Lawrence. Jacksonville upgraded the receiving room and defense, which gives the Jags a chance. Travis Hunter is part of both as a backup receiver and starting left corner. The Dallas Cowboys (15) are going all in, but as talented as the offense is with Dak Prescott throwing to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, the defense will not win a championship.

A soft schedule and QB Jordan Love gives the Green Bay Packers (16) the edge in a tightly packed NFC North. The Packers are hopeful All-Pro DE Micah Parsons returns from his knee injury a month into the season. The Packers will have to supplant the Chicago Bears (17) at the top of the division. The Bears traded one of QB Caleb Williams' favorite targets (D.J. Moore) and did not do much to upgrade the offensive line. Look for a regression from last year's 11 wins. The Minnesota Vikings (18) will have something to say about the division. But that depends a lot on QB Kyler Murray, who is getting a fresh start after six losing seasons, in seven years, in Arizona.

The Pittsburgh Steelers (19) have one of the best defensive lines in the NFL. Good thing when you are counting on 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers to lead the offense.

The only reason the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (20) have a chance at the playoffs is because somebody has to win the NFC South. The division will keep alive the tradition of sending a below .500 team to the postseason.

The future better be bright (and we're talking Dolphins)

Are the Indianapolis Colts (21) the team that started last season 8-2 or finished 0-7? And although that partly depends on the health of QB Daniel Jones, the answer probably is somewhere in the middle. The Washington Commanders (22) went from 12 wins in 2024 to 5 last year. QB Jayden Daniels suffering an elbow injury did not help. Although Daniels appears to be the future, he needs help and losing LT Laremy Tunsil for a good portion, if not all, of the season to a torn triceps is a big blow. The Carolina Panthers (23) made the playoffs at 8-9 last year. Again, the NFC South. So, there always is a chance.

The New York Giants (24) are counting on new coach John Harbaugh to save them. The problem is he has a QB in Jaxson Dart, who was pulled for in-game concussions at least five times last year. Lamar Jackson is not walking through that door for Harbaugh. Speaking of injury prone QBs, the Atlanta Falcons (25) brought in Tua Tagovailoa as insurance for Michael Penix, who is coming off a serious ACL injury. RB Bijan Robinson can only do so much.

The New Orleans Saints (25) have very little going for them other than they are in the NFC South. Have we said the NFC South is bad? For the Las Vegas Raiders (27) , this entire season is about what is best for QB Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick in 2026. That is why Kirk Cousins was brought in to mentor and hold down the position until Mendoza is ready. The Tennessee Titans (28) are going to have to find out if their former first overall pick in 2025, QB Cam Ward, is the answer. The former Miami Hurricane struggled mightily in his rookie year.

For the New York Jets (29) , who brought in QB Geno Smith to improve a dreadful passing game, the only hope is in a slew of future draft picks, including three in the 2027 first round. All you need to know about the Cleveland Browns (30) is they named Deshaun Watson the starting QB and traded reigning Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett.

The outlook for the Miami Dolphins (31) was pretty dismal, and then we saw them play three preseason games. Now, it's even worse. The Arizona Cardinals (32) will turn to QB Carson Beck, the third-round pick from Miami, at some point during the season to replace career backup and journeyman Jacoby Brissett, the former Dwyer standout.

articles.title: Rich Eisen previews Broncos’ season with 4 burning questions
articles.summary: Rich Eisen previews the Denver Broncos' upcoming season with four burning questions.
articles.body:
We have reached the final stretch before the start of the NFL regular season and optimism for the coming campaign remains high within Broncos Country.

The Denver Broncos are a trendy Super Bowl pick this year after coming close to the Big Game last season. However, much like last season, the team has many doubters, mostly related to having to play a first-place schedule and the likelihood that there won't be as many one-score wins as there were last year (11).

Rich Eisen has been previewing the upcoming season team by team and recently, on The Rich Eisen Show , he conducted his preview on the Broncos with four major questions.

Rich Eisen has four questions regarding the 2026 Broncos

1. What in the world does Sean Payton not calling the plays look like?

This is one of the biggest questions anyone has in relation to the Broncos this season. Sean Payton, whether he's the head coach or not, has been calling plays his entire career. He has turned those duties over to Davis Webb this season, but there are many people who feel that Payton will still have a hand in it. That could be. But one thing that is being overlooked is that Webb is the guy who really has the closer relationship with Bo Nix and may have an even better understanding than Payton of the best situations to put him in.

Webb as the play-caller could be what makes or breaks the Broncos in 2026, but it should be seen as a major positive, at least to start the season.

The biggest addition to the roster the Broncos made this offseason, by far, was trading for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. Having an explosive player on offense was the team's biggest glaring need over the last couple of seasons and the team addressed that.

"What burst to the offense will we see from No. 17?" asked Eisen. "The Broncos have not really had anyone like him... in the Sean Payton world."

It is exciting to look forward to what Waddle can bring this team in terms of offensive production, but ultimately, how his presence improves the players around him by opening things up will determine his ultimate value.

3. Can the Broncos defense hit 70 sacks?

The Broncos have led the league in sacks in each of the last two seasons and last year they finished with a huge number of 68. The all-time record for sacks in a season is held by the 1984 Chicago Bears, who had 72.

The absence of Jonathon Cooper , and how long that lasts, will have a huge impact on whether or not the Broncos can threaten 70 sacks this season.

4. Can Bo Nix year 3 make him an MVP finalist?

A lot of people will answer this question with an immediate "no," as there is this belief by many detractors that Bo Nix isn't that good and the Broncos win games in spite of him . That's simply not true. Nix is the only quarterback in NFL history with 50+ passing touchdowns and 10+ scrimmage touchdowns in his first two years in the league. John Elway didn't do that. Josh Allen didn't do that. No one else has ever done that.

The best players on the best teams are the guys who are in the league MVP conversation, so there is no reason to think that Nix won't be in that discussion if the Broncos have another season like they did in 2025.

articles.title: ESPN predicts Titans will draft edge rusher in first round of 2027 NFL Draft
articles.summary: ESPN predicts the Tennessee Titans will draft edge rusher Dylan Stewart out of South Carolina with the No. 6 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.
articles.body:
There is no question that this season is a rebuilding year for the Tennessee Titans . Quarterback Cam Ward needs another year to develop, and he can work on developing chemistry with Tennessee's first-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, wide receiver Carnell Tate. Tony Pollard is back for another year as the lead running back, while they must also figure out who their best defensive players are.

But it is never too early to look to the future at the 2027 NFL Draft. In ESPN 's mock draft from analyst Jordan Reid, Tennessee is projected to pick edge rusher Dylan Stewart out of South Carolina with the No. 6 overall pick.

First, it's worth noting when the Titans are projected to make their pick. There are no projected trades affecting when Tennessee is selecting their pick, meaning Reid is predicting the Titans to finish the year as the sixth-worst team in the NFL.

Honestly, it is surprising they are outside of the top five since they are still rebuilding. However, it makes sense when considering the teams ahead of them - the Miami Dolphins, Arizona Cardinals, New York Jets, Cleveland Browns and Las Vegas Raiders. All five teams are also rebuilding, and four of them are still trying to figure out who their franchise quarterback will be.

Selecting an edge rusher wouldn't be a bad idea, but it seems unlikely the player will be Dylan Stewart, who has yet to have a productive season in college. Tennessee needs players who have proven they can generate pressure and get sacks; Stewart does not fit that bill. Nonetheless, Jordan Reid believes that is who the Titans will select, and here is his justification for this prediction:

"Even though they picked Keldric Faulk in Round 1 in April, the Titans could use more edge-rush help, especially with Jermaine Johnson II entering the final year of his contract. Few edge-rush prospects have ever possessed Stewart's blend of upfield acceleration, bend and closing speed. The production has yet to match the potential, as Stewart had only 4.5 sacks last season, but the 6-foot-5, 250-pounder has rare tools and already has teams giddy about what he could develop into at the NFL level."

Whether or not they want to select an edge rusher will depend on how their pass rush performs this season and also how deep of an edge rusher class there is in this draft. Robert Saleh is a defensive-minded coach, so he will want an elite defense. Still, there will be other defensive options, especially since in this mock draft, the Titans are the first team to take a defensive player, which is entirely possible given the teams ahead of them and their needs.

articles.title: Christian Gonzalez, Patriots Reportedly Agree to Historic Contract to Be NFL's Highest-Paid CB
articles.summary: The standoff between Christian Gonzalez and the New England Patriots came to an end on the eve of their opening game of the 2026 NFL season against the Seattle Seahawks in a Super Bowl 60 rematch.
articles.body:
The standoff between Christian Gonzalez and the New England Patriots came to an end on the eve of their opening game of the 2026 NFL season against the Seattle Seahawks in a Super Bowl 60 rematch.

According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , the Patriots and Gonzalez have agreed to a four-year, $135 million extension that includes $102 million in guaranteed money.

Gonzalez's new contract makes him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history. His deal surpasses the four-year, $132 million (at least $101 million guaranteed) extension Devon Witherspoon got from the Seahawks last month.

Will a non-QB be 2027's No. 1 pick? New NFL mock draft

Gonzalez is also one of 10 defensive players making at least $100 million guaranteed.

The 23-year-old was previously signed through the 2027 season after New England exercised the fifth-year option on his rookie contract.

He's the latest standout corner to receive a hefty deal, as the Seattle Seahawks agreed to a four-year extension worth $132 million with Devon Witherspoon on Aug. 15.

Gonzalez's new contract doesn't come as a large surprise, as Patriots owner Robert Kraft previously confirmed that the team made him a historic offer.

"We love Christian Gonzalez. We love him as a player, as a person, and that's why we've made an offer to him to make him the highest-paid player to ever play that position in the NFL," Kraft said on July 25, per ESPN's Mike Reiss . "And coincidentally, it is the highest contract in Patriots franchise history. So we're glad we drafted him, he's developed here, and we hope he'll be with us for a long time."

Gonzalez also expressed a desire to sign a new deal with New England on June 9.

"Of course, I want to be here. I've said this multiple times," Gonzalez told reporters . "I've been drafted here. I want to be rewarded as a Patriot. I love this town. I love this city. So of course I want to be here."

The Patriots initially selected Gonzalez with the No. 17 overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft.

While he appeared to be starting his career on a high note, his promising rookie season came to an end after just four games due to a shoulder injury .

Gonzalez picked up right where he left off during his sophomore season in 2024, appearing in 16 contests and earning a Second Team All-Pro selection . He finished with 11 passes defended and two interceptions.

During his 2025 campaign, he served as a key piece on a Patriots defense that ranked No. 4 in the NFL by allowing a mere 18.8 points per game.

Gonzalez racked up 69 tackles, 10 passes defended and one tackle for loss across 14 games last season. He allowed a mere 64.4 passer rating when targeted, according to Pro Football Focus .

His stellar season extended to the playoffs, recording seven passes defended in four postseason games while helping New England advance to the Super Bowl.

As the Patriots look to remain a contender in 2026, they secured Gonzalez's future with the team.

articles.title: Derrick Henry Makes Bold Quote on Super Bowl Motivation Heading into 3rd Ravens Season
articles.summary: Heading into his 11th NFL season and third with the Baltimore Ravens, Derrick Henry is ready to hoist the Lombardi Trophy for the first time in his career.
articles.body:
Heading into his 11th NFL season and third with the Baltimore Ravens, Derrick Henry is ready to hoist the Lombardi Trophy for the first time in his career.

Appearing on The Lounge podcast (h/t Ryan Mink of BaltimoreRavens.com ), Henry explained his entire focus for the 2026 season is on helping the Ravens win a Super Bowl:

"It would be crazy for me to say I played with Lamar Jackson and we didn't win no championships. I cannot have that. I do not want that to be a thing. We've got to do it. ... I want to win a Super Bowl. That's a big motivation. I just want to be able to feel that feeling. I'm tired of watching. Every year, I'm tired of being at home on the couch watching. I want to be a part of it. That's what's motivating me right now. I'm going to keep going until we get to that point. We have the 2026 season to get that accomplished."

Late Additions Who Could Influence Super Bowl Hopes 💪

Despite playing a position that typically has a short shelf life in the NFL, Henry has bucked that trend by putting together two of the best years of his career in his first two seasons in Baltimore.

Henry has averaged 1,758 rushing yards and 16 rushing touchdowns per season since the start of 2024. His individual success has not helped the Ravens get over the hump to this point.

Baltimore made the playoffs in Henry's first season before losing to the Buffalo Bills in the AFC Divisional Round. Last season saw the Ravens lose four of their last six games to miss the playoffs for just the second time since 2018.

The 2026 campaign marks the start of a new era for the Ravens with Jesse Minter taking over as head coach after John Harbaugh's 18-year tenure. Many of the roster pieces, including Henry and Lamar Jackson, that have made the team so successful remain in place.

Since winning Super Bowl 47 during the 2012 season, the Ravens have only reached the AFC Championship Game once in the last 13 years. They are a combined 0-4 in the playoffs against the Bills, Kansas City Chiefs and Cincinnati Bengals since 2020.

Henry and the Ravens will kickoff the 2026 season on Sunday when they take on the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium.

Its impact is being felt across locker rooms, front offices and media circles as coaches and executives rethink how they handle professional relationships. An ESPN report says some league figures now feel they are being watched more closely, with the episode raising difficult questions about trust, perception and boundaries around NFL teams.Mike Vrabel-Dianna Russini controversy puts NFL coaches on alertThe controversy surrounding New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel and former NFL reporter Dianna Russini has created an unusual level of anxiety among coaches heading into the 2026 season.ESPN spoke with coaches, players, reporters and league executives, many of whom requested anonymity. Their accounts suggest the story has become more than offseason gossip. For some inside the league, it has become a reminder that private interactions can quickly become public narratives.One assistant coach described the atmosphere bluntly."All the coaches are under surveillance right now, all the s--t with Vrabel," one assistant coach from another NFL team told ESPN.Another assistant coach said the fallout had made him more careful when dealing with female colleagues and reporters. The concern, he explained, is not simply about what happens, but how an interaction might look to others."It's the insinuation; you gotta watch yourself because players, coaches, people are looking at you, like, 'Are you in a relationship?'" he said.That concern highlights one of the biggest consequences of the episode. NFL coaches operate in a world where long road trips, late nights and constant media access are routine. A situation that might once have remained private can now attract intense scrutiny.NFL teams rethink relationships with reportersThe ESPN report also found that the controversy reached team front offices, with at least one organization reviewing how it would respond if a similar situation created a crisis.That development matters because NFL teams are increasingly aware that reputation can become a competitive issue. articles.title: Top Week 1 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Matchup Plays and Sleepers for Opening Games
articles.summary: The opening week can be a tricky one for fantasy managers to navigate. Bona fide fantasy stars like Ja'Marr Chase, Jahmyr Gibbs, and Brock Bowers should be in opening lineups, of course, but it's difficult to know which mid-level options are worth starting.
articles.body:
The opening week can be a tricky one for fantasy managers to navigate. Bona fide fantasy stars like Ja'Marr Chase, Jahmyr Gibbs, and Brock Bowers should be in opening lineups, of course, but it's difficult to know which mid-level options are worth starting.

With flex players and streamers, it's usually best to go with the best matchups. At this point in the season, though, it's impossible to know exactly what those matchups are.

However, we can make educated guesses based on last year's results, depth charts, and projected roles. We'll do exactly that here before diving into a few sleepers to consider.

Start: Omarion Hampton, RB, Los Angeles Chargers

Los Angeles Chargers running back Omarion Hampton showed a ton of promise when he was healthy as a rookie last season. He's healthy now, as are standout offensive tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater.

Los Angeles may open up with a pass-heavy approach just to get Justin Herbert and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel on the same page. At some point, however, it is going to look to salt the game away with a heavy dose of Hampton against a questionable Arizona Cardinals defense.

Arizona ranked 24th in yards per carry allowed last season and surrendered 19 touchdowns on the ground. The Cardinals didn't significantly improve their defense during the offseason either, meaning Hampton should be facing an attractive matchup.

Sit: Jadarian Price, RB, Seattle Seahawks

The Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots will kick off Week 1 with a rematch of Super Bowl LX. The Seahawks dominated that game, while running back Kenneth Walker III raced to MVP honors with 159 scrimmage yards.

With Walker now in Kansas City and Zach Charbonnet on injured reserve, this should be a great matchup for Seahawks rookie Jadarian Price , right? Well, perhaps not.

The Patriots ranked sixth in rushing yards allowed last season and allowed just 11 touchdowns on the ground. There's also a very good chance that returning running back George Holani sees a large amount of the third-down and receiving work early in the season.

Waiting a week to try out Price would be the prudent move for managers with other RB options.

Start: Tre Tucker, WR, Las Vegas Raiders

While Las Vegas Raiders receiver Tre Tucker isn't a must-start for Week 1, he's a strong option for managers looking to stream a wideout in the flex. He was Las Vegas' top wide receiver a year ago (696 yards, 5 TDs) and should get a significant boost from new quarterback Kirk Cousins.

Tucker should also have a favorable matchup against a Miami Dolphins defense that could be one of the worst in the league. Miami's roster lacks overall talent, as evidenced by the fact that it added seven players off waivers during roster cuts.

The fact that Ashton Jeanty is still dealing with an ankle sprain could also prevent the Raiders from being as run-heavy as they otherwise might be against a team of the Dolphins' caliber.

Week 1 Waiver Wire Top Fantasy Pickups and Drops on Yahoo, Sleeper

While Tucker remains the Raiders' top wide receiver, the Buffalo Bills have a new one in trade acquisition D.J. Moore. The former Chicago Bears standout should give Josh Allen a viable No. 1 option, though fans shouldn't expect a ton of production in Week 1.

Buffalo will open with a brutal matchup against the Houston Texans and last year's top-ranked defense. In the matchup, Moore is likely to draw a heavy dose of star Texans cornerback Derek Stingley Jr.

While Khalil Shakir led the Bills with an impressive eight receptions and 110 yards in last year's matchup with Houston, fans shouldn't expect a similar performance out of Moore. When pressed, Allen is likely to target familiar faces like Shakir instead of his newest perimeter weapon.

New Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray will get his first start against the rival Green Bay Packers. While Green Bay's defense was largely solid in 2025, it won't have star pass-rusher Micah Parsons (ACL) to open the season.

Murray will get to throw to top-tier targets like Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and Jauan Jennings, and his scrambling ability should provide a high fantasy ceiling. Rostered in just 38.7 percent of fantasy leagues, he's a sneaky starting option and worth scooping up for managers in a pinch at QB.

Mike Washington Jr., RB, Las Vegas Raiders

Jeanty's injury is a big reason to consider Raiders rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. Even if Jeanty was at 100 percent, though, Washington would have flex value as a committee back in Klint Kubiak's offense.

Against a Dolphins defense that ranked 28th in yards per carry allowed last season, Washington is a strong flex option and a smart pickup if available. He's rostered in 24 percent of fantasy leagues.

The Texans acquired Kayshon Boutte in a late-summer trade, and he should quickly slot in as their No. 2 receiver. With Buffalo focusing on limiting No. 1 wideout Nico Collins, Boutte has solid sleeper value right away.

Buffalo ranked an impressive fifth in yards per pass attempt allowed last season. However, the transition to Jim Leonhard's 3-4 defense could leave some opportunities for Boutte, who is rostered in nine percent of leagues.

articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver D.K. Metcalf pushed back against criticism of the personalities of the star quarterbacks he's worked with in a recent interview with The Athletic's Jonathan Jones.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver D.K. Metcalf pushed back against criticism of the personalities of the star quarterbacks he's worked with in a recent interview with The Athletic's Jonathan Jones .

Metcalf defended both Russell Wilson, with whom he played for three seasons on the Seattle Seahawks, as well as his current teammate Aaron Rodgers ahead of the Steelers' Sunday season opener.

"I never liked when people called Russ corny," Metcalf said, per Jones. "Because what if that's just Russ? Why does it have to be a specific title to it? Russ is always great to me. Never looked at him as corny. He's a great father, great football player, a great friend, great brother, great businessman, but I never looked at him as corny.

Metcalf continued, per Jones, "Same way as I never look at Aaron as an a--hole. He's just a perfectionist. He's done everything at a high clip his whole life. And if you don't do that around him, then you're lazy in his eyes.

"So you either have to meet people where they are, or don't hang around them. So people just have to just accept people for who they are."

Metcalf's comments to Jones comes after both he and Rodgers discussed their relationship in August appearances on ESPN's Pat McAfee Show.

Rodgers told McAfee last month the two had bonded when the quarterback hosted some of his pass catchers this summer in Idaho.

"Last year, compared to this year, it felt like we were teammates, and this year we're actually really close friends," Rodgers said.

Metcalf told McAfee on the same episode, "We definitely got the chance to get to know each other on a more intimate level this offseason.

"Last year we were still teammates. I didn't want to mess up, he didn't want to mess up, we were just not on the same page a couple times. But this is going to be special this year."

Metcalf missed two games last season but still led Steelers receivers in targets (99), catches (59), receiving yards (850) and receiving touchdowns (six).

The Steelers will now hope improved chemistry between Metcalf and Rodgers can lead to an even more productive campaign that will help this team break its decade-long playoff win drought in what Rodgers has said will be his final NFL season. That push begins Sunday with a 1 p.m. ET home game against Tua Tagovailoa and the Atlanta Falcons.

articles.title: DK Metcalf Says He Wasn't 'Sour' Over Seahawks' Super Bowl Win After Trade to Steelers
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers star receiver DK Metcalf had to watch as his old Seattle Seahawks won the Super Bowl less than a year after trading him, but he has no regrets.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers star receiver DK Metcalf had to watch as his old Seattle Seahawks won the Super Bowl less than a year after trading him, but he has no regrets.

While speaking to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, Metcalf made it clear that he has no ill feelings toward the Seahawks after they granted his request to be traded before the 2025 season.

"I live with my decisions every day… they're very well thought-out decisions to where I know the consequences, know my benefits from every decision that I make," Metcalf said. "I got brothers on (the Seahawks), still friends on the team. So I congratulated them, but nobody's sour over an ex unless you really miss them. So no, I wasn't sour."

The Steelers sent a 2025 second-round draft pick to the Seahawks to acquire Metcalf, who was then signed to a four-year contract extension that made him one of the highest-paid receivers in the league at $33 million per year.

The 28-year-old reportedly pushed to be shipped out of the Pacific Northwest because he "grew frustrated with his role under one-and-done offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb" in 2024. Jones noted that Seattle was open to fulfilling Metcalf's trade request "in part because the Seahawks suspected they would have to pay Jaxon Smith-Njigba sooner rather than later."

Metcalf had a solid year in his first season in Pittsburgh, finishing with 99 catches for 850 yards and six touchdowns in 15 games. However, that paled in comparison to the success Seattle achieved, as Smith-Njigba was named NFL Offensive Player of the Year as the team went on to hoist the Lombardi Trophy for the second time in franchise history.

It can be expected that Metcalf will be extra motivated to help lead the Steelers to title contention this year. Pittsburgh will open the 2026 season on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons.

articles.title: Steelers' DK Metcalf Explains Belief in Conspiracy Theory That Antarctica is 'Another World'
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers has always been known for his outlandish beliefs, but it now appears that he's not the biggest conspiracy theorist on his team.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers has always been known for his outlandish beliefs, but it now appears that he's not the biggest conspiracy theorist on his team.

Steelers star receiver DK Metcalf told The Athletic's Jonathan Jones that the title belongs to him.

"Yeah, I'm a big conspiracy theorist," Metcalf told Jones. "Shout out to my quarterback."

Late Additions Who Could Influence Super Bowl Hopes 💪

Metcalf then revealed that one of his most curious theories is his belief that Antarctica is "another world."

"I think there is another civilization inside of Earth," he said.

The 28-year-old said the source of the conspiracy lies in access to the Arctic continent.

"You can go to Alaska. You could go to the North Pole," Metcalf said. "But why not Antarctica? Why can't you just book a trip to Antarctica?"

Of course, you can book a trip to Antarctica. Tourism usually takes place between November and March and typically requires ships leaving from South America to travel to the Antarctic Peninsula. There are no commercial airports on the continent, and those that do exist are controlled by the government, which further feeds into Metcalf's theories.

"Why is there a secret meeting — well, it's not secret," Metcalf says, "but why is there a meeting between every world leader of every country in Antarctica, specifically?"

There are no records of such meetings taking place. But if there were, they wouldn't be much of a secret, right?

Metcalf and the Steelers will open the 2026 season on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons, so he will have to put his conspiracy theories to rest over the next few months.

articles.title: Could Joe Milton III use his painful Dallas Cowboys exit as motivation to prove he deserves a bigger role in the NFL?
articles.summary: NFL News: Joe Milton III did not hide his disappointment after the Dallas Cowboys released him last week. The decision came after a preseason competition with S.
articles.body: Joe Milton III did not hide his disappointment after the Dallas Cowboys released him last week. The decision came after a preseason competition with Sam Howell for the backup quarterback spot behind Dak Prescott. Still, Milton refused to let the setback change how he sees himself. After clearing waivers and returning to the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad, he now has another chance to keep developing and show that he belongs in a bigger NFL role.Dallas Cowboys’ decision surprised Joe Milton III, but he has no plans to doubt himselfThe roster cut clearly surprised Milton, but it did not appear to damage his confidence. Instead of questioning his ability, the quarterback made it clear that his belief in himself remains strong."Nah, I'm still the best quarterback in my eyes," Milton said. "So, it is what it is. It's just something you gotta live with, take it to the chin."That confidence will be important as Milton enters another uncertain stage of his young NFL career. He has played only a handful of regular-season games, making every opportunity to show what he can do especially important.His preseason performance gave the Dallas Cowboys plenty to consider. Milton completed 29 of 43 passes for 378 yards and three touchdowns. Sam Howell completed 27 of 40 passes for 314 yards and also accounted for three touchdowns.Dallas ultimately chose Howell as Dak Prescott’s backup, but Milton’s numbers showed that the competition was not one-sided.His biggest advantage continues to be his arm strength. Milton has the physical tools to make difficult throws down the field, but becoming a trusted NFL quarterback requires more than a powerful arm. His development, decision-making and consistency will determine whether he can turn that natural ability into a lasting opportunity.The practice squad gives him time to work on those areas.Joe Milton III sees Dak Prescott and Dallas Cowboys as the right place to keep buildingMilton could have ended up with another team after clearing waivers. Instead, he chose to return to Dallas, largely because of the relationships he has built inside the organization.Having Dak Prescott around also gives him access to a veteran quarterback who understands what it takes to survive and succeed in the NFL."I've got Dak in my (QB) room. A lot of places don't have a true vet that's been a starter in this league since they got in. Having him in the room is one of those ways that I know for sure I'll be taken care of, as far as my knowledge and development of the game – and football talk for sure."That kind of environment could be valuable for Milton. A practice squad position may not carry the attention of a backup quarterback job, but it can provide an important period of growth. He can prepare against the Dallas Cowboys’ defense, learn from the coaching staff and remain ready if the team needs him.Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer also made it clear that the team was pleased Milton made it through waivers."Quarterback rooms around the league are pretty crowded right now, but he’s certainly talented enough to get claimed," Schottenheimer said. "It’s our good fortune that he wasn’t."Prescott has also shown support for Milton, praising his talent, work ethic and progress. That backing gives Milton another reason to stay patient while continuing to compete.For now, Milton’s path is not the one he expected when training camp began. He wanted the backup job and instead found himself off the active roster before returning to the practice squad.But the story is far from finished."Everything happens for a reason," Milton argued.Now, his task is to make those words mean something. If he keeps improving and stays prepared, an unexpected chance could eventually come his way. The Dallas Cowboys may have cut him once, but Milton clearly has no intention of letting that decision define his NFL career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Joe Burrow Predicted as NFL MVP in Poll of Execs, Full List of Award Winners Ahead 2026 Season
articles.summary: On the eve of the 2026 NFL season kicking off, Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is predicted to win the MVP award by people who work in the league.
articles.body:
On the eve of the 2026 NFL season kicking off, Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is predicted to win the MVP award by people who work in the league.

Per a survey of NFL executives and scouts conducted by ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Burrow was a slight favorite for the MVP over Justin Herbert and Josh Allen.

Here is the full list of predicted award winners from the ESPN survey.

Perhaps sensing some unease from Burrow after missing the playoffs in each of the past three seasons, the Bengals acted aggressively this offseason in a way that is not in keeping with their usual business model.

Cincinnati traded the No. 10 overall pick in the 2026 draft to the New York Giants for Dexter Lawrence to boost its defensive line talent. The trade marked the first time since 1989 the Bengals didn't have a first-round pick.

The Bengals also spent $125 million to add Boye Mafe, Bryan Cook and Jonathan Allen to their defense in free agency.

Burrow has two fourth-place finishes in MVP voting in 2022 and '24, but around those two years are injury-plagued seasons that kept him off the field for long stretches. He played just eight games in 2025 and 10 in 2023, causing one AFC executive to tell Fowler they don't trust him to stay healthy to be an MVP contender.

"I'm done banking on Burrow because of the injuries," the exec said. "I would, if not for health issues. Stafford won't get it again, Mahomes is coming back from injury, and even though you can't count out Lamar, he's taken a step back. Allen is the safest bet."

The two major individual awards outside of the MVP are predicted to go to Jahmyr Gibbs (Offensive Player of the Year) and Will Anderson Jr. (Defensive Player of the Year).

Trading David Montgomery opened up even more carries for Gibbs in the Detroit Lions' offense. He had already moved into being the lead back last season, starting all 17 games and recording a career-high 320 touches.

Anderson and Myles Garrett were the only players who received votes in the Defensive Player of the Year category. They finished first and second last season with Garrett winning after setting an NFL record with 23 sacks.

One thing that could hurt Garrett, aside from the difficulty of repeating as an award winner unless you improve on your stats from the previous year, is the Los Angeles Rams defense being so loaded up front that it could split some of the voting from that group.

The Houston Texans are also incredibly deep on defense, but Anderson is the unquestioned leader of the pass-rush. It could also help that he has yet to win and is an ascending superstar for a team expected to be among the best in the AFC.

As the start of the 2026 season draws nearer, the Dallas Cowboys are setting themselves up to be one of the most active teams in the trade market.

While speaking on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Tuesday, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones confirmed that the team recently restructured contracts to create more cap space, which would make it easier to execute a potential trade this season.

"That does show that we have really serious room to make a trade if we wanted to right now," Jones said.

ESPN's Todd Archer reported last week that the Cowboys created a little over $19 million in salary cap space by restructuring the contracts of veteran defensive tackle Kenny Clark, cornerback DaRon Bland and tight end Jake Ferguson. Dallas also recently acquired offensive tackle Broderick Jones and a 2027 fourth-round pick from the Pittsburgh Steelers in exchange for 2027 third- and sixth-round picks.

While the Cowboys' dealings have left them with only five picks in next year's draft, Jones said Tuesday that he would be open to trading more of those picks to upgrade the roster because he's focused on this year's team. He added that Dallas would likely look for improvements on defense, but the team isn't in a rush to make a move.

"The best way for me to answer that is not timing-wise, right on something this morning or this week," Jones said . "But if you look at it generally speaking, we're in play. And that's the best way to describe it."

articles.title: Mike Washington Jr. and the Best Week 1 Fantasy Football Waiver-Wire Pickups
articles.summary: The 2026 fantasy football is finally about to get underway. While your league has likely drafted by now, there's still time to tweak your roster and get things in tip-top shape before the new campaign kicks off.
articles.body:
The 2026 fantasy football is finally about to get underway. While your league has likely drafted by now, there's still time to tweak your roster and get things in tip-top shape before the new campaign kicks off.

The final weeks of preseason and training camp brought about a series of sweeping changes, many of which will impact the upcoming fantasy season. With so many players getting traded, cut, claimed off waivers, going down with injuries or returning from them, depth charts across the league saw a flurry of changes in a short span.

Fantasy projections have been altered accordingly. Some of the players you drafted, especially those in the later rounds, may no longer be worth rostering. Other players who went undrafted can now be considered must-add pieces.

With that in mind, let's highlight some unheralded players—available in 40 percent or more of Yahoo! fantasy leagues—that have enough upside to warrant a roster spot and could potentially even start for your team in Week 1.

Fantasy points and rankings courtesy of FantasyPros using PPR data.

QB Daniel Jones, Indianapolis Colts (25 Percent Rostered)

Fantasy managers are understandably wary of Daniel Jones going into the new season. The Indianapolis Colts' QB1 ended the 2025 campaign on a sour note, with his production waning while he battled injuries before landing on the IR with an Achilles tear.

Despite the rough finish, Jones was a fantasy football revelation for the first half of last season. He scored 22-plus points in five of the first eight games and rated as the QB5 through 10 weeks of play.

Jones also proved to have a stable floor during his first season in Indy, scoring 15.8 points or more in all but one game prior to his season-ending injury. As long as he bounces back from the Achilles ailment and retains some of the mobility that helped him pile up points last year, the veteran will remain a solid play in 2026.

The Colts open the season with a decent matchup against the Baltimore Ravens, a team that allowed an average of 17.7 points per game to opposing signal-callers last year. With Alec Pierce back after an extended offseason absence, Jones will have all of his key weapons available and ready for what should be a high-scoring showdown at Lucas Oil Stadium.

If you are planning to stream quarterbacks this season, aren't satisfied with the QB you drafted or simply want to add depth behind your preferred starter, Jones is a good choice. He'll be one of the hottest Week 2 waiver wire targets with a strong showing in the opener, so get ahead of the rush by adding him now.

RB Mike Washington Jr., Las Vegas Raiders (56 Percent Rostered)

Mike Washington Jr. was largely off the fantasy radar going into his first NFL season. The Las Vegas Raiders' fourth-round rookie was set to open his career stuck behind lead back Ashton Jeanty on the depth chart and wasn't projected to get enough touches to move the needle in Year 1.

That changed when Jeanty went down with an ankle sprain during a practice session last month. While the initial reports were highly concerning, the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport revealed that the sophomore standout's ankle issue is "more high than low". Still, Jeanty has been sidelined for several weeks since picking up the ailment and his availability for Week 1 remains a question.

Regardless of whether Jeanty gives it a go or not, Washington should be considered a must-add player in nearly all formats.

If Jeanty is officially declared out, Washington instantly vaults onto the RB1 radar. He'll take over the lion's share of volume usually allocated to Jeanty, who racked up a hefty 321 touches on his way to an RB11 finish as a rookie last year. Dylan Laube will also be in the mix, but Washington will be the clear backfield leader in any game Jeanty misses.

Should Jeanty play but be on a pitch count, Washington still has some RB3/flex appeal. He had a strong preseason—rushing for 119 yards on just 15 carries—and proved he can produce with limited touches. As a jumbo-sized, 6'2", 228-pound RB who ran a blistering 4.33-second 40-yard dash at the combine, the sky appears to be the limit for this intriguing prospect.

Even if you don't plan to start Washington when the Raiders host the Miami Dolphins in Week 1, there are few second-string backs with the same combination of upside and potential opportunity that the rookie currently has. Washington is worth adding for his handcuff value alone and shouldn't be left on waivers.

RB Jonah Coleman, Denver Broncos (34 Percent Rostered)

The Denver Broncos are opening the 2026 NFL season with a crowded backfield, but it may not be long before this becomes a two-man platoon.

With J.K. Dobbins having one of the most unfortunate injury histories of any modern player, shrewd fantasy managers will want to scoop backup Jonah Coleman and keep him waiting in the wings for what seems to be an inevitable injury to Denver's starting running back.

Dobbins has been highly productive when available throughout his six years in the NFL, but he's never made it through an entire campaign unscathed. He was sidelined for seven games last season—his first with the Broncos—and four the year prior. The 27-year-old also sat the entire 2021 campaign and missed all but one game in 2023.

While RJ Harvey took control of Denver's backfield during Dobbins' absence in 2025, Coleman figures to be the main beneficiary if the veteran goes down again this year.

Coleman, a fourth-round pick in the 2026 draft, quickly stood out in training camp for his immense potential. He only saw action in one preseason contest—picking up 24 yards on four totes—before head coach Sean Payton declared he had seen enough to know the rookie would play a role for the squad.

Yahoo! Sports' Nate Tice broke down the patience and skill Coleman showed during his brief exhibition appearance against the Atlanta Falcons:

Expect Coleman to burst out as Denver's RB1 if Dobbins misses time. He boasts a similar toolkit to Dobbins and can seamlessly replace the starter when given the opportunity. Harvey will remain a factor, but is a more likely to continue performing his third-down, pass-catching duties after an up-and-down showing in a more feature role last year.

Although Coleman probably won't see more than a handful of touches in Denver's upcoming Monday Night Football opener against the rival Kansas City Chiefs, he's an ideal waiver target to stash and deploy later in the season once attrition sets in.

WR Kayshon Boutte, Houston Texans (21 Percent Rostered)

Kayshon Boutte wound up being the odd man out in the New England Patriots' deep receiving corps this offseason, but landed in an ideal spot after getting shipped to the Houston Texans before cutdown day.

Boutte will now have ample opportunity to showcase his skills on a squad that became downright desperate for receiving help last month. When projected No. 2 wideout Jayden Higgins went down with a season-ending ACL tear several weeks ago, Houston's brass sifted through the free-agent pile before opting to make a move for Boutte.

Although he hasn't had much time to learn a new system and build rapport with quarterback C.J. Stroud and his other new teammates, Boutte should still play a large role in Houston's Week 1 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. He's the most proven receiver the team has outside of No. 1 wideout Nico Collins and will contend with slot wideout Jaylin Noel and tight end Dalton Schultz for looks behind the superstar.

While Boutte's season-long outlook is murky due to the impending return of Tank Dell (who is opening 2026 on the PUP list), he'll still have at least four games to establish himself as one of Stroud's go-to weapons.

At his best, Boutte is a field-stretching playmaker who can rack up big gains and scores. He finished 2025 as the WR51 and disappeared at times, but also racked up five top-25 finishes over his first 11 appearances last season. Boutte truly shined between Weeks 6-8, a three-game stretch in which he tallied 223 yards and four touchdowns on 10 catches.

If Boutte earns Stroud's trust and becomes the team's primary deep threat, he'll have a chance to put up some week-winning numbers early in the season. Any manager seeking upside from a free-agent wideout could do far worse than adding Boutte and deploying him as their WR3 this week.

TE Brenton Strange, Jacksonville Jaguars (31 Percent Rostered)

Brenton Strange had an up-and-down season last year, one in which he established himself as a viable weapon for the Jacksonville Jaguars but also missed five games with injury and largely lacked consistency. If he can put it all together in 2026, Strange has top-10 potential.

In the 12 games he suited up for last year, Strange recorded 46 catches for 540 yards and three touchdowns. His 9.8 points per game ranked as the 15th highest amongst tight ends who participated in at least 10 contests in 2025, showing clear upside ahead of a pivotal fourth NFL season.

While Strange will have to contend with Brian Thomas Jr., Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Travis Hunter for looks, his 6'4", 253-pound size, impressive athleticism and strong hands will help him surge up Jacksonville's pecking order if he's given a chance.

Even if he's utilized mostly as a safety valve and red area target by quarterback Trevor Lawrence, Strange still should have a decent amount of fantasy value—especially the dearth of appealing options at the position—for managers seeking a bye week or injury fill-in.

Don't expect a blistering start from Strange, but he's a fantastic stash choice with undeniable breakout potential. An injury in Jacksonville's receiving corps could be all it takes for him to move out of TE2 range and into the upper echelon of the position.

articles.title: Who are Tom Brady’s three sisters? Meet Maureen, Julie, and Nancy Brady
articles.summary: NFL News: Before Tom Brady became a seven-time Super Bowl champion and one of the world’s most renowned athletes, he was simply the youngest child in a fiercely.
articles.body: Before Tom Brady became a seven-time Super Bowl champion and one of the world’s most renowned athletes, he was simply the youngest child in a fiercely competitive California family of six.“My life began in a large household where five people were eagerly awaiting the birth of their first son and brother. I was raised in a family where the expectations were high, and the failures were inexcusable,” Brady wrote in a high school English essay in October 1994.Brady grew up with three older sisters - Maureen, Julie, and Nancy - and their ambitious influence on him was far greater than many fans realize. The English essay Brady wrote in high school, titled “The Way My Sisters Influenced Me,” offers a surprisingly emotional glimpse into his relationship with his three older sisters.In it, Tom confessed how often people identified him through his sisters before he had accomplished his own athletic identity. He duly noted that he wanted to be “recognized as an individual and not as another ‘Brady.’”That sentiment makes his sisters’ stories particularly intriguing!Tom Brady’s oldest sister Maureen Brady was the family’s first sports starTom Brady and his three sisters were born to Thomas Brady Sr. and Galynn Patricia Brady [nee Johnson]. They tried to introduce their four children to music and fine arts through piano, guitar, and dance lessons, but all four gravitated toward sports. With all four children involved in sports, Tom Sr. noted, they played a combined 315 games in one year.Maureen Brady, born in 1970, the eldest sibling, was already an accomplished athlete before her younger brother became popular. She played collegiate softball at Fresno State University from 1992 to 1995. An All-American pitcher, she helped the Bulldogs reach the Women’s College World Series in 1992 and 1994.Maureen has two daughters with Brian Timmons. The couple got divorced in 2010. Maureen’s eldest, Maya, plays softball for the Oklahoma City Spark of the Athletes Unlimited Softball League [AUSL]. Her youngest, Hannah, recently made her college volleyball debut at Michigan, for which Tom Brady commented, “So proud of you,” on Instagram.Maureen Brady’s athletic reputation was so powerful that Tom was sometimes known merely as her younger brother.That detail makes Tom’s English essay particularly poignant: long before he became the NFL G.O.A.T., “Tom Brady,” he tried to carve out his own identity in a family already filled with accomplished athletes.Julie Brady and Nancy Brady also carved their own pathsJulie Brady, Tom’s second-oldest sister, also played sports in college, like her elder sister, Maureen. From childhood, Tom and Julie were often called twins. They share the same birthday - August 3. But they are three years apart: Julie was born in 1974, and Tom was born in 1977.She tried out for the soccer team at St. Mary’s College as a walk-on and later earned a scholarship. She is married to Kevin Youkilis, a former Major League Baseball player who played third base for the Boston Red Sox. They married in April 2012. Julie and her husband share two sons, Zachary and Jeremy. Julie also has a daughter, Jordan, from a previous relationship.Nancy Brady, Tom’s youngest of three older sisters, was born in 1976. Tom was born a year later, in 1977. Nancy received a scholarship to play softball at UC Berkeley.According to the Fresno State Bulldogs website, Nancy attended graduate school in Boston at 35.Publicly available professional information on LinkedIn also identifies a Nancy Brady associated with JSI in the Boston area for 11 years as senior technical advisor. She previously worked for Tom Brady Management, Pfizer, and Accordia Global Health Foundation.Tom Brady’s emotional high school English essayAt the end of Tom’s 1994 English essay, the NFL legend wrote,“No matter what awards people may give me or what records I might break, the most meaningful thing to me is when I succeed in not only athletics, but life, the individuals who will always be there to support and recognize me will be my three sisters, Maureen, Julie, and Nancy.And hopefully, just maybe, one day, people will walk up to them and say, ‘Aren’t you Tommy’s sister?’ or ‘Hey, where is your brother?’ Maybe….”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Brandon Graham Makes Final Decision on NFL Future amid Speculation About Eagles Return
articles.summary: After coming out of retirement to help the Philadelphia Eagles last season, Brandon Graham is stepping away from football once again.
articles.body:
After coming out of retirement to help the Philadelphia Eagles last season, Brandon Graham is stepping away from football once again.

Graham announced at an event in Philadelphia on Tuesday that he is "officially done" playing after 16 seasons.

There had been indications from Graham throughout the summer that this was coming. He said on NFL Network's Good Morning Football in July that he would prefer to be on the roster at the start of training camp rather than come in midway through the season if he was going to play.

"I would love to start in the beginning if I can," Graham said (h/t Ed Kracz of SI.com), "but if training camp doesn't happen, I think I'll probably wrap it up after that."

Graham's initial retirement announcemen t came in March 2025, one month after the Eagles defeated the Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl 59.

"I gave everything I had in this. I have no regrets," Graham said at the time. "My life has been forever changed because of this magical place."

An injury to Nolan Smith Jr. and Za'Darius Smith's surprise in-season retirement led to the Eagles calling Graham about making a comeback. He officially rejoined the team prior to Week 8 last October.

Graham played 10 games last season, including the Eagles' 23-19 playoff loss to the San Francisco 49ers. He recorded three sacks and three quarterback hits in the regular season.

A first-round pick in the 2010 draft, Graham spent his entire career in Philadelphia. He ranks third in franchise history with 79.5 sacks, trailing only Reggie White (124) and Trent Cole (85.5). His 215 games played rank first in Eagles history.

Graham won two Super Bowl titles with the Eagles. His strip sack on Tom Brady late in the fourth quarter of Super Bowl 52 helped secure Philadelphia's 41-33 victory over the New England Patriots.

articles.title: Todd Monken Details Talk with Deshaun Watson After Viral Comments About Browns Fans
articles.summary: After Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson went viral for his comments disparaging the team's fans, first-year head coach Todd Monken knew he had to address the situation.
articles.body:
After Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson went viral for his comments disparaging the team's fans, first-year head coach Todd Monken knew he had to address the situation.

During an appearance on 92.3 The Fan in Cleveland on Tuesday, Monken detailed the conversation he had with Watson after the signal-caller declared that Browns fans were "disrespectful" for booing him during the team's second preseason game.

"I mean, after that game — I'll just say during the game and then after the game, certainly Deshaun was not in a great headspace. Let's be real honest about it," Monken said (h/t Myles Simmons of Pro Football Talk). "He said it after the game, he was frustrated, and didn't particularly play well. And we don't coach well and call it well around him. So, we certainly all have to own that."

DK's Wild Antarctica Conspiracy Theory 🤨

Report: Pats' Gonzalez to Be Highest-Paid CB

Monken went on to admit that he questioned Watson's confidence following his remarks, but the 30-year-old assured him that the instance wasn't indicative of his mindset.

"I looked at it more along the lines of a speed bump and just a blip on the radar more than the norm of what I had seen over the course of the five months being here, in terms of his confidence, how hard he's worked to get back to where he's at today," Monken said. "And he did, he came to me right after that, him and I had a good conversation, and he said, 'I'm not sure I handled that the right way. But I did have things that were on my heart.' And I asked him, I said, 'Do you feel like you've gotten rid of it?' Because it's one thing to say it. It's another thing to really believe it, that OK, I needed to get this off my chest, it's over, I just want to go out there and play great football. I've worked awfully hard to get back."

Monken added that he's confident Watson has moved past the situation, and he's making sure the three-time Pro Bowler knows that he has the support of the entire franchise.

"The only way you're going to get the best out of your players is to have a verbal contract that says, I've got your back. I've got your back, I've got you," Monken said. "That's what we've done with Deshaun, and we look forward to playing this weekend."

Watson was named Cleveland's starting quarterback over Shedeur Sanders for Sunday's season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Monken made it clear that he didn't consider the fans' opinion when he decided between Watson and Sanders, but he understood the reaction afterward.

"[T]he fans just want us to win and play good football. So, I do understand some of the frustration," Monken said. "I do think that, unfortunately, it's viewed a little bit like hate and hope — is really the way I put it. The fans really just want hope. And Deshaun, over the years that he's been here, has frustrated the fans and, certainly, himself in terms of wanting to play better for the Cleveland fans and the organization. And I get where they're coming from, but ultimately, any great fanbase like ours wants to win, wants to see a great product on the field. And that's what we're aiming to do starting this week and as long as I'm the head coach here."

articles.title: How the Patrick Mahomes-Travis Kelce business empire reveals a totally new way NFL stars are planning for life after football
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce are still suiting up for the Kansas City Chiefs in 2026. But quietly, methodically, they are also building something .
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce are still suiting up for the Kansas City Chiefs in 2026. But quietly, methodically, they are also building something that has very little to do with fourth-quarter drives or Super Bowl rings. Between MLB ownership stakes, a Formula One team, a high-end steakhouse, a media empire, and a string of startup investments, these two have constructed a financial architecture that most NFL players never attempt while still active. The blueprint they are writing is not just for themselves. It is changing what post-football wealth can look like for the next generation.What businesses do Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce actually own together?The most visible joint move is 1587 Prime, their Kansas City steakhouse that opened in September 2025. The name comes from combining their jersey numbers, 15 for Mahomes and 87 for Kelce, and the restaurant sits inside the Loews Kansas City Hotel, spanning nearly 10,000 square feet across two floors. It has already earned nominations across four categories in the 2026 Kansas City Favorites awards, including Fine Dining, Steak, Wine Selection, and Specialty Cocktails. Not bad for a place that has been open less than a year.But 1587 Prime is only one piece of a much larger puzzle they built together. Both are minority investors in the Alpine Formula One team through Otro Capital, a deal that also brought in Rory McIlroy and Anthony Joshua. Mahomes said at the time that he could not pass up the chance to invest in a sport gaining fast momentum in the US. "It's an exciting time for the sport and this is an opportunity to bring our shared values to the world stage," Mahomes said. Kelce added: "Our shared passion for excellence and innovation forms the cornerstone of this partnership."How are Mahomes and Kelce planning for life after the NFL through sports ownership?This is where the strategy gets genuinely interesting. Both men now own pieces of Major League Baseball franchises, in rival teams no less. Mahomes became the youngest part-owner in professional sports in 2020 when he purchased a stake in the Kansas City Royals at age 24. Beyond baseball, his ownership portfolio includes Sporting KC in MLS and the Kansas City Current in the NWSL.Kelce followed a parallel path in May 2026, buying a minority stake in the Cleveland Guardians, the city where he was born and raised. "I have so much love for this city," Kelce told ESPN. "I say it all the time: I'm just a kid from the Heights living the dream." He also made clear this is not a vanity move. "I've been lucky enough to have a front-row seat to good ownership in my career, and I know the best teams prioritize culture. Everyone is there to play their role, and right now, I'm here to observe and learn."What makes this so different from the celebrity endorsement model that defined athlete income for decades is the intentionality behind it. These are not guys slapping their names on a product for a check. They are taking board-room-level positions in growing sports properties and learning ownership from the inside, while they are still playing.What can other NFL stars learn from the Mahomes–Kelce investment approach?The honest answer is: quite a lot. Most NFL players earn the bulk of their money between ages 22 and 32, then spend the following decades trying to preserve it. Mahomes and Kelce are doing something structurally smarter. They are converting their peak-fame window into equity stakes in industries, sports franchises, media, and consumer brands, that compound in value long after their playing careers end.Mahomes has acknowledged that his investment experience directly influences how he thinks, including when it came to restructuring his own contract. "Being able to be in those meetings and negotiations helps me have an understanding for the business side of things," he said. He also credits Kelce's influence, noting that his teammate has shown him the value of staying open-minded about expanding his role beyond football.Kelce's individual portfolio backs that up. Beyond Alpine and the Guardians, he invested in Six Flags through JANA Partners in October 2025, holds a stake in Recover 180, and co-owns the New Heights podcast with his brother Jason, which signed a multi-year deal with Amazon. "We're both as competitive as it gets, so you know there will be some bragging rights on the line when we play our division games," Kelce said, referencing the AL Central rivalry between the Guardians and Royals. But behind the banter is a genuine alignment in strategy. Two active NFL players who have studied ownership closely and are now making decisions from that side of the table, before football is even done with them.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL Week 1 Vegas power rankings: Los Angeles Rams are the clear No. 1 team
articles.summary: Our NFL handicapper gives his power rating for all 32 teams.
articles.body:
A useful tool for handicapping any sport is making a list of power ratings. It serves as a baseline resource for how to price games by providing a theoretical against the spread number.

The table below shows all 32 NFL teams, ranked by their corresponding power rating. The ranking is simple: a 1-32 order of the best teams in the NFL. The rating is used by matching any two teams up against one another, find the difference in the numbers, factor in a home field advantage (standard 1.5 points in the NFL) and boom - you are now projecting a spread.

Let's look at my preseason NFL power ratings, provide an example on how to use them, and then quickly discuss the potential pitfalls of this process to be aware of, and find a bet to action.

1. Los Angeles Rams (+7.4) are playing the San Francisco 49ers (+3.3)

The difference spits out Rams -4.1 (aka Rams favored by 4.1 points). Since there is no home-field advantage because of the international game, we don't factor in home field. Currently, BetMGM lists the odds at Rams -3.5 (-112).

2. The Arizona Cardinals (-6.5) are playing at the Los Angeles Chargers (+2.4)

The difference spits out Chargers -8.9. This game is in Los Angeles, so factor in a 1.5-point home-field advantage for the Chargers and we are at Los Angeles -10.4. Currently BetMGM lists the odds at Chargers -10.5 (-108).

These two examples are pretty aligned with the market and don't signify a big betting edge. Occasionally, you will find examples where there is a discrepancy worth betting into.

Before placing a bet based on ratings, be aware of these potential pitfalls that a rating system can't perfectly encapsulate.

Injuries: Ratings published here on Tuesdays are static for the week, but injuries are not. Injured players might not be accurately factored in. This is especially true for mid-week practice injuries and players who are listed as questionable — their availability will impact the spread. Always check the injury report and ask yourself if that explains the gap between the number you can bet at a sportsbook and the number the rating system spits out.

Matchup-based advantages: A rating system allows you to match up any two teams in the NFL, but it doesn't account for which team has the best rushing attack going against a team with the worst run defense. Those matchup specifics will sway spread numbers a bit as well. If you feel a team has a specific edge, and the rating system matches the spread, that can also be an edge you see and bet into.

Key numbers: Specific to the NFL, line moves at certain numbers are so valuable that we should factor that into ratings system calculations. The easiest example is the half point line moving onto or off of the 3 is worth three times as much as the half point onto or off of the 2. If a team is two points better than its opponent, and we need to add in home-field advantage to the priced favorite, we should probably expect to stop at -3 and not go to -3.5. Maybe the line is -3 (-115).

Bet worth actioning: Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Cincinnati Bengals (-4, 50.5)

According to my preseason power ratings, the Bengals are +1 and the Bucs are -0.1. This creates a 1.1-point gap in the Bengals' favor. They are also playing at home, so let's go ahead and tack on another 1.5 points. Bengals -2.6 is what the system spits out. Since the Buccaneers are +4 here, that is the side I want.

We also know the Bengals under head coach Zac Taylor have always struggled early in the season. Taylor is 2-5 in Week 1 in his seven seasons, and that extends to a 3-11 record when factoring in Week 2 as well. Inversely, the opposite is true for Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles: Bowles is 4-0 in Week 1 and 8-0 in Weeks 1 and 2 at the helm of Tampa Bay.

While I am not a big trends bettor, understanding how a coach prepares his team during training camp for being ready early in the season bears some significance to me. The main injury news that hangs in the balance is to Bucs WR Emeka Egbuka. He is dealing with a toe injury that reports have been very coy about; it is hard to figure out the severity.

My inclination is that he will play, and while he might be limited, his availability probably means the spread should not be impacted.

articles.title: Eagles legend Brandon Graham announces retirement after 16 seasons
articles.summary: Brandon Graham announced his retirement for a second time, ending a franchise-record 16-season career spent entirely with the Philadelphia Eagles
articles.body:
Brandon Graham is retiring from the NFL again, officially ending one of the most accomplished and beloved careers in Philadelphia Eagles history.

Graham announced his retirement Tuesday after 16 seasons, according to Zach Berman of The Athletic . The 38-year-old spent his entire career with Philadelphia, becoming a two-time Super Bowl champion and the longest-tenured player in franchise history . Graham retired following the Eagles' Super Bowl win over the Patriots after 15 seasons in the NFL, but Philadelphia convinced him to return from retirement last October. He recorded three sacks and eight tackles in nine games and played a handful of snaps on the interior to help replace an injured Jalen Carter.

His two-sack performance against the Las Vegas Raiders made him the oldest player in Eagles history to record a sack.

Philadelphia released Graham in June in what was described as a procedural move, leaving open the possibility of another return. Graham expressed interest in playing a 17th season and participating in a full training camp, but the Eagles entered September with a younger and deeper group of edge defenders.

The No. 13 overall pick in the 2010 NFL Draft, Graham appeared in 215 regular-season games and recorded 79.5 sacks and 128 tackles for loss. His career required patience after early injuries and criticism, but he eventually developed into one of the franchise's most dependable defenders and respected leaders.

Graham's defining play came in Super Bowl LII when he stripped Tom Brady late in the fourth quarter. The turnover helped Philadelphia secure a 41-33 victory over the New England Patriots and its first Super Bowl title. He later returned from a torn triceps to appear in Super Bowl LIX, becoming one of four players to participate in both of Philadelphia's championship victories.

Graham's playing career is over, but his relationship with the Eagles is expected to continue. He has discussed remaining around the organization as a mentor while exploring opportunities in media and other areas of football.

After one comeback and 16 seasons in Midnight Green, Graham is finally ready for his next chapter.
