articles.title: Ranking Backup QBs Who Could Be Traded During the 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Every team has a quarterback plan heading into the 2026 NFL season, but those could quickly go awry once play begins later this week. With injuries and ineffectiveness sure to strike the position, it won't be long before clubs start looking to bring in a new passer via the trade market.
articles.body:
Every team has a quarterback plan heading into the 2026 NFL season, but those could quickly go awry once play begins later this week. With injuries and ineffectiveness sure to strike the position, it won't be long before clubs start looking to bring in a new passer via the trade market.

There are several backups who currently stand out for their high potential to be dealt prior to the 2026 trade deadline on November 11. Whether they lost their starting job due to a free-agent or draft acquisition, are entering the final year of their contract or fell out of favor with a new coaching staff, these depth options are strong candidates to get a fresh start this year.

While their value can vary wildly—teams won't hesitate to ask for early-round picks for promising backups who have fared well during their limited on-field opportunities, while those who struggled across multiple starts won't command much capital in return—and potential suitors could shift drastically based on how the early portion of the 2026 campaign shakes out, there are five QBs who have a better chance than the rest to be moved at some point in the coming months.

With that in mind, here's a ranked look (based on contract value, current role and projected asking price) at the backup QBs who could be traded in 2026.

Mac Jones has been the constant target of trade rumors this offseason, with the quarterback himself recently addressing them by saying "anything's possible" when asked about the potential to be moved during an appearance on The Rich Eisen Show . It's hardly a surprise that he's a hot trade target, given the strong stretch of play he put on tape when given the opportunity last year.

Things looked bleak for the San Francisco 49ers when it was revealed that they would be without Brock Purdy for an extended stretch due to injury. Despite not having their starting quarterback for much of the 2025 campaign's first half, the team remained in contention and ultimately made the playoffs thanks to Jones' impressive turn under center.

After being cast aside by both the New England Patriots—the team that took him in the first round of the 2021 draft—and Jacksonville Jaguars, Jones showed that he still has the stuff to be a starter in the NFL. The signal-caller completed an impressive 69.6 percent of his throws for 2,151 yards and 13 touchdowns while leading San Francisco to a 5-3 record across eight starts.

Jones became the latest quarterback to study under renowned 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan, benefiting from his tutelage and innovative system. San Francisco has been a Super Bowl contender for much of the coach's nine years at the helm largely thanks to his ability to maximize the talent of his passers and put them in a position to succeed.

While Jones finally fared well in the Bay Area after several shaky years in the league, teams may be leery about trading for the 28-year-old. He had ample opportunity to put it all together in both New England and Jacksonville—starting 46 games over his first four NFL seasons—but never emerged as a consistent, quality performer outside of a promising rookie year.

Desperate clubs will still roll the dice on Jones being able to continue playing at a high level outside of San Francisco. Expect him to generate strong interest from any club that loses it starter, but the Niners will likely ask a high price as they can afford to hang onto Jones as insurance against another Purdy injury.

No. 4: Spencer Rattler, New Orleans Saints

The New Orleans Saints appear to have found their quarterback of the future in Tyler Shough. Shough's rapid ascent coincided with Spencer Rattler falling out of favor in the Big Easy, opening the door for the third-year signal-caller to be traded this season.

Rattler had a rocky rookie season after the Saints selected him on Day 3 of the 2024 draft. He failed to win any of his six starts and only completed 57 percent of his throws, but wound up getting the first opportunity to start under new head coach Kellen Moore last season. While his accuracy noticeably improved, the results remained the same as Rattler won just one of his eight starts.

With Shough taking the reins and finding success almost immediately, Rattler was left competing with free-agent pickup Zach Wilson for backup duties in 2026. He looked decent in the preseason—completing 68.2 percent of his passes for 262 yards in three games—but didn't do enough to truly distinguish himself from Wilson (who tallied 293 yards and a touchdown through the air on a 65 percent completion rate).

While Rattler did fare well to make the final roster and even drew some trade interest this offseason, his tenure as a potential starter in New Orleans is over barring Shough suffering a major, unexpected regression or injury.

Rattler's value should only go up when a quarterback inevitably goes down with injury early in the season. The Saints can afford to be patient until then, maximizing the potential return for the signal-caller and slotting Wilson into the primary backup role if a trade does occur.

No. 3: Tanner McKee, Philadelphia Eagles

The Philadelphia Eagles made the bold decision to keep four passers on their active roster on cutdown day, but it may not be long before their quarterbacks room gets a bit less crowded.

The Eagles opted to keep a pair of newcomers in veteran Andy Dalton and rookie fifth-rounder Cole Payton in addition to entrenched starter Jalen Hurts and promising backup Tanner McKee. While Payton is a developmental prospect who isn't likely to see any action in 2026, McKee and Dalton could both conceivably handle the QB2 job.

While both backup candidates struggled at times during the preseason, Dalton should have an edge when it comes to sticking around for the duration of the campaign due to his wealth of experience in the NFL. He was a nine-year starter for the Cincinnati Bengals—making three Pro Bowls in that span—before entering the second act of his career, one that has seen him assume a backup role for five different clubs over the last seven seasons.

McKee has a far higher ceiling than his 38-year-old counterpart, but has yet to see much meaningful action at the professional level and was on the roster bubble this offseason for a poor stretch of play. He's only seen action in six games since the Eagles selected him in the sixth round of the 2023 draft and has drawn just two starts in his three seasons.

While McKee displayed enough promise in these regular season contests to make him a desirable trade target for rival franchises, he also failed cement his status as Hurts' primary backup during the 2026 offseason.

As tantalizing as McKee's ceiling may be, the Eagles find themselves in a position where they can move on from this polarizing 26-year-old while still having a proven old hand to work directly behind Hurts and a long-term project to bring along if they keep both Dalton and Payton.

Given that McKee is entering the final year of his rookie deal and reportedly drew strong offers that included a Day 2 pick at last season's trade deadline, it's hard to see Philadelphia's brass choosing to keep him beyond November.

DK's Wild Antarctica Conspiracy Theory 🤨

Report: Pats' Gonzalez to Be Highest-Paid CB

The Cleveland Browns' quarterback carousel continued its endless spin this offseason when Deshaun Watson beat out Shedeur Sanders for the QB1 job. The two-man competition left little room for Dillon Gabriel to establish himself as anything more than a deep backup on the fringes of the roster.

While Gabriel—a third-round pick in the 2025 draft—was selected ahead of Sanders last year and got an opportunity to start after Cleveland traded Joe Flacco early in the campaign, he failed to spark the club's listless offense. Gabriel went just 1-5 across six starts, finishing his rookie season with modest marks that included a 59.5 percent completion rate, 937 passing yards and seven passing touchdowns.

Gabriel won't even open 2026 on the active roster, beginning instead on the IR as he works to return from a back injury suffered in the team's preseason finale. The Browns still opted to keep three passers on the active roster, with rookie sixth-rounder Taylen Green slotting in as their QB3.

Green fared well in his lone preseason showing and is shaping up to be far more appealing developmental prospect than Gabriel, who appears to be the odd man out in Cleveland's quarterback room. Gabriel's trade value isn't much at this point, but the team could still recoup some capital from a club looking to pad out its depth and take on a rehabilitation project for pennies on the dollar.

The Minnesota Vikings' J.J. McCarthy era could be at an end after the much-maligned quarterback failed to beat out Kyler Murray for the starting job in training camp. McCarthy never lived up to the lofty expectations set by his No. 10 overall selection in the 2024 draft, with injuries and poor play leading the team to acquire the competition he ultimately lost out to this offseason.

With McCarthy missing all of his rookie season with a torn meniscus and struggling immensely upon being handed the QB1 role last year, it seemed it was only a matter of time before he fell out of favor in the Twin Cities. A dreadful preseason showing and more injuries led McCarthy to drop behind Carson Wentz on the depth chart and has opened the door for a trade.

According to NFL insider Jason La Canfora , executives around the league widely expect the Vikings to move on once they receive an offer they like for McCarthy. This could include a conditional pick based on playing time.

Although the Vikings won't be able to recoup anything close to the draft capital they gave up to acquire McCarthy, the team could get a clean break from the disappointing passer in exchange for a late-round draft pick (or a couple cases of Gatorade as Mark Schlereth suggested on his podcast). Such a move would also give McCarthy a chance to start fresh and potentially rehabilitate his career in another system.

McCarthy may not be a prized commodity at this stage of his career, but he's still just 23 years old and has some potential to turn things around. He showed flashes of brilliance during his short stint as Minnesota's starter, including leading an epic fourth-quarter comeback over the rival Chicago Bears in his NFL debut last year.

With Murray locked in as the starter and Wentz a capable backup who can keep the ship steady when called upon, the Vikings shouldn't hesitate to take whatever they can get for Nine if another team is willing to take him.

articles.title: Why is the NFL starting on a Wednesday in 2026? NFL Week 1 schedule
articles.summary: Why is the NFL starting the season on a Wednesday in 2026? Explaining change in NFL schedule, with a complete list of how to watch NFL Week 1 games.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL Week 1 schedule is kicking off on Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026, which is different from its recent typical Thursday opening-game kickoff.

Why is the NFL starting the season on a Wednesday in 2026?

The Super Bowl rematch between the Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots is on Wednesday because the NFL has scheduled the Los Angeles Rams to take on the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia on Friday, Sept. 11.

But due to the time difference, that game is being played at 5:35 p.m. MST (8:35 p.m. ET) on Thursday, Sept. 10 in the United States, prompting the league to move the opener up a day.

The Patriots vs. Seahawks game will start at 5:20 p.m. MST (8:20 p.m. ET) on Wednesday at Lumen Field in Seattle.

It is the first time since 2012 that the NFL is not starting its season on a Thursday.

In 2012, the NFL shifted its opener to a Wednesday to accommodate President Barack Obama's Democratic National Convention speech.

The NFL is scheduled to have nine international games in 2026, with the Rams vs. 49ers game the first.

It will be the first time the NFL has a game in Australia.

articles.title: Titans' Robert Saleh Defended by Solomon Thomas Ahead of Jets Revenge Game, Firing Was 'So Wrong'
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh will be opening his first season with his new team against his old team, the New York Jets, on Sunday in Nashville.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh will be opening his first season with his new team against his old team, the New York Jets, on Sunday in Nashville.

The Jets fired Saleh five games into his fourth season in 2024, capping a 20-36 stint in New York. However, Titans defensive tackle Solomon Thomas has been a staunch defender of Saleh, having played under him for nearly his entire 10-year career.

Thomas had this to say on the matter in an exclusive interview with Nick Suss of the Tennessean :

DK's Wild Antarctica Conspiracy Theory 🤨

Report: Pats' Gonzalez to Be Highest-Paid CB

"I've been with Saleh eight out of my 10 years. I have a lot of love for him and I've been around him a lot. How that ended was so wrong. We were tied for first in our division and our head coach gets fired. In no situation would that ever make sense. I'm sorry. I will talk about that. Just the fact that he has so many former Jets here just shows that guys love playing for him. They know what he's about to do here and they want to be a part of it."

The 2024 Jets bounced back from a season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers by beating the Titans and New England Patriots to move to 2-1. However, the offense stalled in back-to-back losses to the Denver Broncos and Minnesota Vikings, dropping the team to 2-3 and a game back of the first-place Buffalo Bills.

Saleh was fired two days after the Vikings game, but he excelled as the San Francisco 49ers' defensive coordinator last year and returned as a head coach in 2026.

Thomas played under Saleh as the 49ers' defensive coordinator (2017-2020, 2025) and the Jets' head coach (2022-2024), and now he's with him in Nashville.

"I think there was such a disconnect based on what was portrayed from the front office to the locker room," Thomas said of Saleh's Jets tenure. "I don't really like talking about anything other than football. But I've never really been in a place where more was said out of the front office than out of the locker room. And said as a distraction. And it was really unfortunate because our locker room was really the opposite of what was going on in the front office."

Regardless of the opponent on the other sideline, it's crucially important for the Titans to get the Saleh era off to a victory against a beatable opponent in the Jets, who are coming off a 3-14 season. Tennessee just went 3-14 itself but overhauled the coaching staff and invested around second-year quarterback (and 2025 NFL draft top pick) Cam Ward, so there's hope for improvements in town.

Kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday from Nissan Stadium.

articles.title: 2026 NFL season predictions for Super Bowl winner, MVP, top surprises and disappointments
articles.summary: This season, we think we have it figured out. Well, most of us anyway.
articles.body:
At this time last year, nobody was picking the Seattle Seahawks to win a Super Bowl. One of the things that makes the NFL great is unpredictability.

This season, we think we have it figured out. Well, most of us anyway.

The Los Angeles Rams come into the season as a clear Super Bowl favorite. But not all of our Yahoo Sports experts picked L.A. to win it all. The Rams were the most popular Super Bowl pick, but not even the unanimous pick to win the NFC West.

It was unanimous in predicting the AFC North and AFC South. And nearly so for the Bills in the AFC East, which means we're collectively expecting some regression with the defending conference champion Patriots. Joining the Bills as near unanimous favorites are the Dallas Cowboys in the NFC East. Yes, we can collectively see your eyes rolling at that one.

The Rams will be the must-watch team of this season, after acquiring Myles Garrett and getting Aaron Donald to return after two seasons in retirement. But other teams could keep it from being a one-team race, as we see in our season predictions.

The picks for awards are spread out. There were four players predicted to win MVP, including multiple picks for Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott, who has never won the award.

NFL Coach of the Year was even more spread out, with six different coaches getting mentions and nobody getting more than two votes.

The Rams trading for Myles Garrett was the offseason's biggest move, however, he's not our collective favorite to win Defensive Player of the Year.

And finally, our hot take section. Enjoy our boasts, gripes and wild guesses for what's in store for the 2026 season.

articles.title: Buffalo Bills: Joe Brady under pressure to lead Josh Allen to Super Bowl, says Phoebe Schecter
articles.summary: Sky Sports NFL's Phoebe Schecter questions whether this could finally be the year one of Josh Allen or Joe Burrow win a Super Bowl; watch the Bills open their 2026 campaign against the Houston Texans live on Sky Sports NFL from 6pm on Sunday as the race to Super Bowl 61 begins
articles.body:
The Bills renew their Super Bowl quest this season having endured more playoff agony earlier this year when they were beaten by the Denver Broncos in overtime of January's Divisional Round clash.

It had been deemed a premature end to one of their best opportunities yet to end prolonged Super Bowl agony, with Patrick Mahomes' Kansas City Chiefs absent from the playoffs for the first time since 2014 and the likes of Lamar Jackson and Joe Burrow also nowhere to be seen.

Sean McDermott was subsequently fired after nine campaigns in charge, with Brady being promoted to head coach from his post as offensive coordinator.

"Josh Allen will have had a say with Joe Brady coming in and taking on that role," said former Bills coach Schecter on Inside the Huddle .

"It was just odd at the time in terms of how it happened, that kind of firing in order to promote from within."

Allen's Bills have suffered four Divisional Round exits and two AFC Championship Game defeats since 2020, four of those losses coming against the Chiefs.

Their 73 victories in that period are notably more than any other team in the league, Allen consistently spearheading one of football's most potent offenses.

Buffalo sought to strengthen their quarterback's aerial options by trading for Chicago Bears wide receiver DJ Moore, who hasn't recorded a 1,000-yard campaign since 2023.

"You look at what DJ Moore does for the team when you bring him in," Schecter continued. "That already elevates an offense that has never really had a star receiver.

"They're still trying to keep that mentality, but you pair that with a fantastic running game. We saw James Cook all last season taking over, but it's a very interesting that we have so many teams in the AFC that were having a similar conversation around with your Lamar Jacksons, your Joe Burrows - when will these guys win a Super Bowl?

"That of all the teams the most pressure is on Joe Brady in terms of the expectation is for him to get to a Super Bowl because they've always been the bridesmaid, never the bride.

"It'll be fascinating to see how he manages that pressure, especially as they move deeper into the season. But everyone feels good about it. You've got a new stadium, you've got a new excitement around it and that kind of rejuvenation."

The Bills also hired Jim Leonhard as their new defensive coordinator to oversee a new-look unit that saw the likes of Joey Bosa, AJ Epenesa, Matt Milano and Tre'Davious White depart in the offseason.

"Leonard is the key to this whole deal," said Sky Sports NFL's Jeff Reinebold. "Jim Leonard is a brilliant young coach, and if he can get that defense just a little bit better than it's been and better balance, this could be Buffalo's year."

Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals stake their only claim as NFL 'nearly men' alongside both Allen's Bills and Jackson's Baltimore Ravens.

The Bengals have missed out on the playoffs for three straight years and managed just one postseason appearance since their defeat to the Los Angeles Rams at Super Bowl LVI.

Burrow, who has missed 16 games through injury over the last three seasons, demanded urgency from his team this offseason as he seeks to maximise, when healthy, one of the most explosive passing attacks in football.

"He said it himself, we all know he's been injured so many times coming into this season, or they've had some big injury within the team, but the time is now and they've got to chase that success," said Schecter.

"The biggest complaint last year was how they were putting so much money into this defense and they were probably the worst performing defense.

"But bringing in Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen, you get Kyle Dugger from the Patriots, you've got a smart defense. You've got a safety who can now organise everybody.

"They've got to be able to go down and capitalise on having this fantastic trio on offense with Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins and go attack it. This city needs it.

"The fan base are so desperate for it and you don't have an endless clock with Joe Burrow, especially seeing his injury rate over the past few seasons."
